content.thinking: I've settled on a design plan built around an on-call rota board: coloured shift bars, a "now" line, and a 24-hour clock motif, using Archivo's variable width axis and a marigold/teal/violet palette for people with red reserved for alerts. The layout centers on a full-width hero schedule with orchestrated draw-in animation, and I've swapped out generic SaaS card kits and a dark hero for an unboxed icon grid and a daylight/night split instead.

content.text:
I've written the Rotaline landing page as one `index.html` in the working directory. I checked it in headless Chrome screenshots at 1440px and 390px wide, including the open mobile menu, annual pricing and an expanded FAQ answer. It has no horizontal overflow at 390px; the product schedule scrolls sideways inside its own frame.

**Design direction.** The look is built around an on-call rota board.
- **Colour:** a cool light background with dark navy text. Three colours (marigold, teal and violet) always mean the people on the rota, so they appear in the schedule bars, the logo mark, the "How it works" line and the avatars. Red is used only for the "now" marker and for incidents. Marigold is also the main button colour.
- **Type:** one typeface, Archivo, set wider for headings and at normal width for body text.
- **Hero:** this is the one bold element. It is a working-looking week view for a "Platform team" with Primary, Secondary, a follow-the-sun Database rotation and Payments. A red line marks the current time, and a side panel shows the next handoff, from Marcus to Jun, with an open incident carried over. On load the shift bars draw in from left to right and the handoff panel settles in. That is the only automatic animation, and it is turned off for people who have reduced motion enabled.
- **Everything else is deliberately quiet.** The features have line icons rather than boxed cards. Numbered markers appear only in "How it works", because that is the one real sequence. The results sit in a dark navy band, and the Team plan is shown dark with a "Most popular" badge.

**How each section behaves:**
- **Navigation:** on screens under 900px the nav becomes a menu button. It opens a panel, closes on Escape or when you pick a link, and announces whether it is open to screen readers.
- **Pricing toggle:** switches Team between $9 and $7 and Business between $16 and $13, and updates the "billed monthly / billed annually" note. Screen readers are told about the change.
- **FAQ:** uses the browser's built-in expand and collapse, with an animated plus/minus icon.
- **Email form:** checks the address in the browser. It shows a plain error ("Enter an email address like name@company.com.") or a confirmation; nothing is actually sent.
- **Accessibility:** keyboard focus is visible everywhere, and the schedule illustration has a full text description for screen readers.

**Copy I added:** section headings, one-line plan descriptions, a footnote explaining how the results were measured, and the five FAQ answers. All the names, numbers and copy you supplied are used as given.

**Before publishing:**
- **Pricing claims:** I wrote two pricing claims beyond your brief: the "save up to 22%" label (from $9 to $7), and a line saying customers are only charged for people on at least one rotation. Remove the second one if it doesn't match your intended billing.
- **Font loading:** Archivo loads from Google Fonts. My headless Chrome couldn't fetch it reliably here, so for the screenshots I pointed a temporary copy at downloaded font files; your `index.html` is unchanged. In a normal browser the page shows text straight away in a system font and switches to Archivo once it loads. Opened from disk with no internet, it stays in the system font, which is wider so headings will wrap differently.

**Design direction.** The look is built around an on-call rota board.
- **Colour:** a cool light background with dark navy text. Three colours (marigold, teal and violet) always mean the people on the rota, so they appear in the schedule bars, the logo mark, the "How it works" line and the avatars. Red is used only for the "now" marker and for incidents. Marigold is also the main button colour.
- **Type:** one typeface, Archivo, set wider for headings and at normal width for body text.
- **Hero:** this is the one bold element. It is a working-looking week view for a "Platform team" with Primary, Secondary, a follow-the-sun Database rotation and Payments. A red line marks the current time, and a side panel shows the next handoff, from Marcus to Jun, with an open incident carried over. On load the shift bars draw in from left to right and the handoff panel settles in. That is the only automatic animation, and it is turned off for people who have reduced motion enabled.
- **Everything else is deliberately quiet.** The features have line icons rather than boxed cards. Numbered markers appear only in "How it works", because that is the one real sequence. The results sit in a dark navy band, and the Team plan is shown dark with a "Most popular" badge.

**How each section behaves:**
- **Navigation:** on screens under 900px the nav becomes a menu button. It opens a panel, closes on Escape or when you pick a link, and announces whether it is open to screen readers.
- **Pricing toggle:** switches Team between $9 and $7 and Business between $16 and $13, and updates the "billed monthly / billed annually" note. Screen readers are told about the change.
- **FAQ:** uses the browser's built-in expand and collapse, with an animated plus/minus icon.
- **Email form:** checks the address in the browser. It shows a plain error ("Enter an email address like name@company.com.") or a confirmation; nothing is actually sent.
- **Accessibility:** keyboard focus is visible everywhere, and the schedule illustration has a full text description for screen readers.

**Copy I added:** section headings, one-line plan descriptions, a footnote explaining how the results were measured, and the five FAQ answers. All the names, numbers and copy you supplied are used as given.

**Before publishing:**
- **Pricing claims:** I wrote two pricing claims beyond your brief: the "save up to 22%" label (from $9 to $7), and a line saying customers are only charged for people on at least one rotation. Remove the second one if it doesn't match your intended billing.
- **Font loading:** Archivo loads from Google Fonts. My headless Chrome couldn't fetch it reliably here, so for the screenshots I pointed a temporary copy at downloaded font files; your `index.html` is unchanged. In a normal browser the page shows text straight away in a system font and switches to Archivo once it loads. Opened from disk with no internet, it stays in the system font, which is wider so headings will wrap differently.
